> **A FUTURE `last_obs_date` IS USUALLY CORRECT, NOT A BUG.** Many publishers ship genuine PROJECTIONS: CSO Ireland's `18_Population_Projections` runs to 2057, Estonia's `rahvastik` to 2085, ABS to 2046/2071, UN WPP to 2101, IMF WEO to 2031. `health.py` already separates the two — `frontier` is the furthest period held INCLUDING projections (display only), `newest_obs` filters to periods <= today and is the recency signal — because 28 of 93 units legitimately reported a future frontier. Do NOT "repair" a future date until you have looked at the series key and the year sequence.
>
> What IS a defect: a SENTINEL (9999-12-31, 2999-12-31) or a COUNTER read as a year (years 1, 2, 3 ... contiguous from 1 — no projection starts at year 1). Tell them apart by the key and the sequence, never by the size of the number. See R320/R322 and `tools/audit_impossible_dates.py`, whose bounds (before 1500, after 2200) are deliberately far outside every real projection horizon.

## 3. How it works

**Why this strategy** (registry `strategy_reason`):

> Melodi /data/{FLOW_CODE} supports startPeriod/lastNObservations and the catalog exposes a per-dataflow lastUpdate; gate on lastUpdate and pull startPeriod=last_obs+1 per flow rather than re-paginating all flows.

**Adapter contract** (registry `adapter`):

- `vintage_signal`: Catalog lastUpdate field per dataflow (dataflow/all catalog) compared against a stored per-flow marker; enumerate ~109 flow codes from that catalog.
- `since_param`: startPeriod=<max(obs_date)+1 period> on /data/{FLOW_CODE} (gated by catalog lastUpdate > stored marker).
- `out_paths_note`: Multi-file: one parquet per dataflow at data/clean_full/insee_melodi/{FLOW_CODE}.parquet (~79 files). Merge by read+concat+dedup on (flow,series_key,obs_date); some flows large (DS_BPE* ~25 MB). Add .tmp staging (no atomic write today).
- `rate_note`: No API key (keyless 'libre' plan, Accept: application/json). Documented 30 req/min cap -> RATE_DELAY 2.1s between pages/flows; HTTP 429 -> 60s sleep.

**Fetcher module**: [`updater/strategies/fetchers/insee_melodi.py`](../../updater/strategies/fetchers/insee_melodi.py)

<details><summary>Its own module docstring — the authoritative description, including every defect previously found and why the code looks the way it does</summary>

```
S3 (sdmx_delta) fetcher — INSEE Melodi, France. Keyless SDMX 2.1 catalog.

Layout (set by jobs/ingest_insee_melodi.py): ONE parquet per DATAFLOW under
clean_full/insee_melodi/<FLOW_CODE>.parquet with schema
  flow        : string  (constant within a file — the dataflow code)
  series_key  : string  ("DIM=val:DIM=val:..." over every dimension EXCEPT TIME_PERIOD,
                         sorted by dimension name — exactly the ingester's composite key)
  obs_date    : date32  (parsed from TIME_PERIOD: YYYY->Dec-31, YYYY-Qn->quarter-start,
                         YYYY-MM->month-start, YYYY-MM-DD->that day)
  value       : float64 (first non-null measure's .value)
The dedup identity is (flow, series_key, obs_date).

WHY THIS FETCHER WAS REBUILT (2026-10-16, design reviewed as AR-330, ledger R1588/R1589).
  * 46+ flows were served at EXACTLY one Melodi page (10,000 rows) - all 39 DS_RP_TD_* census tables
    among them - because pagination could end early (a 4xx or an empty page treated as "no more data")
    and nothing checked. INSEE publishes no total, so the store looked complete.
  * Every pass since 2026-10-06 was killed at the 45-minute unit limit: _fetch_flow_obs held every page's
    raw JSON in one list (~1.6 KB per observation, 16 GB runner) and a census flow's "tail"
    (startPeriod = its only year) is the whole flow; Melodi also ignores startPeriod for RP flows.

HOW A PASS RUNS NOW (slots in precedence order, all inside the 35-minute soft stop - R2-7):
  0. operator force: every flow listed in _force_origin.json (once per listing) is sent to needs_origin,
     whatever its status (see STATUSES AND THE OPERATOR below).
  1. identity: one HEAD per served file, compared with _flows.json; a changed object is re-classified and
     any attempt it carries is dropped (a tail never finishes a flow sent to origin - AR-331 X4); a
     missing served object is named in the note.
  2. CLASSIFY (<= 5 min, charged with the probes, their two controls and the page-determinism control):
     an unclassified flow is NEVER written by the walk (R2-2). needs_origin when ANY key-spelling
     partition (dimension-name set + GEO vintage) or the total is an exact positive multiple of 10,000,
     the flow is zero-row/absent, it is in CI_PAGE_MULTIPLE_DELTAS, or the operator forces it. Otherwise a
     one-time page-beyond probe (page floor(S/10,000)+2 of an origin query, S = the DISTINCT normalised
     (key without FREQ and GEO vintage, date) count - R2-1) decides: non-empty means INSEE serves more than
     we hold. An empty probe is NOT proof of completeness.
  3. WALK (until minute 15): the healthy flows, rotated; each is tailed only when INSEE's catalog
     `modified` changed, the catalog read failed, or 30 days passed. Every tail is STAGED like a re-pull;
     one that outgrows one chunk (100 pages) joins the repair queue.
  4. REPAIR (until the soft stop): ONE flow at a time - an in-progress or merge-pending attempt first,
     then needs_origin, then needs_refresh. Pages are parsed at once into Arrow, staged locally and
     uploaded every 100 pages as _repull/<FLOW>/<attempt>/<n>.chunk; the cursor lives in _flows.json.
  A flow is COMPLETE PER INSEE PAGING only when: paging.isLast is True (a full last page is confirmed by an
  empty/400 page+1); there are no duplicates ACROSS pages (within-page duplicates are a parse collision,
  labelled, never a restart - R2-5); the chunk footers sum to the staged rows. Then a measured merge:
  rows new or changed against the stored file decide changed_keys (an idempotent tail derives nothing);
  for an origin pull the stored rows INSEE no longer serves are counted as RESIDUE and KEPT (merge, never
  replace - Q1). Only then is the served file published, then the state, then the chunks deleted.

  While any repair work remains the pass returns `transient_fail` WITH changed_keys (the _giant / PR #151
  precedent): due at the next run, and the merged flows' CSVs are derived this pass. Its note carries the
  counters health and the digest show.

STATE AND STAGING (all through blob - R2 before T0, the local store after): `_flows.json` (this fetcher's
state; conditional writes - see _melodi_state.py), `_force_origin.json` (OPERATOR-owned, read only; its
format is under STATUSES AND THE OPERATOR below), `_repull/<FLOW>/<attempt>/<nnnnn>.chunk`. Local
staging lives beside the bounded-merge spill dir (ECONDL_DUCKDB_TMP), never D:.

STATUSES AND THE OPERATOR (each flow's `status` in `_flows.json`; the note names the stuck ones every pass):
  `unclassified`        not profiled yet (or its served object changed); never written by the walk.
  `legacy`              no exact-multiple partition; probed once with the page-beyond probe; walked.
  `needs_origin`        a full origin pull is queued (a bootstrap rule, a non-empty probe, or the operator).
  `needs_refresh`       a due tail too large for the walk, queued for the repair slot (it may carry a
                        parked attempt).
  `in_progress`         the ONE flow being pulled; its attempt and cursor are in `attempt`.
  `merge_pending`       every page staged, waiting for the merge (it needs its time margin).
  `complete_per_paging` an origin pull ended on isLast with every check met; walked.
  `empty_per_paging`    INSEE serves no observations for it; walked.
  `withdrawn_suspect`   origin page 1 empty over stored rows: withdrawn by INSEE? Stored rows kept.
  `unstable_paging`     3 restarts (pages changed under the attempt); its chunks are deleted.
  `broken`              3 failures with no committed chunk between them, or a pull that parsed nothing;
                        its chunks are deleted.
  The last three are worked by nobody until the operator acts. A flow whose merge is refused is NOT one of
  them: it stays `merge_pending` with every staged chunk, retried each pass, and the note escalates
  (MERGE REFUSED n pass(es), then NEEDS THE OWNER from 3) - a refusal is a condition of the merge, never of
  the paging (AR-330 C11). THE OWNER'S ACTION for NEEDS THE OWNER: read the cause in that note line and fix
  it - a full spill disk (free space where ECONDL_DUCKDB_TMP points, else <repo>/data/_duckdb_spill), the
  bounded merge's memory (AQUEDUCT_BOUNDED_MERGE_MEMORY), the spill cap (the free disk less
  AQUEDUCT_BOUNDED_DISK_RESERVE_BYTES), or a shrink or column refusal (the merged file would lose rows or columns: look at the flow first). The
  merge then retries by itself on a later pass and the count clears. A force does NOT help: it keeps a
  refused ORIGIN pull as it is (a re-pull cannot cure a merge refusal).
  THE OPERATOR'S FILE is `_force_origin.json` (the fetcher never writes it). Two forms of "flows":
      {"flows": ["DS_X", "DS_Y"], "unblock_repair_after_utc": "<iso>"}
      {"flows": {"DS_X": "<iso>", "DS_Y": "<iso>"}, "unblock_repair_after_utc": "<iso>"}
  - A listed flow, in ANY status, drops its attempt (unless that attempt is already an origin pull) and goes
    to `needs_origin`: this is the exit from broken, unstable_paging and withdrawn_suspect.
  - The force is PER FLOW and happens ONCE (recorded as the flow's `forced_key`). In the list form a flow is
    forced once while it stays listed: adding or removing another flow forces nothing again, and neither
    does any other field. To force a flow AGAIN, either use the object form and give that flow a new value
    (only that flow is forced again), or take it off the list for one pass and list it again. A
    top-level `utc` field has no effect.
  - `unblock_repair_after_utc` later than the REPAIR BLOCKED time lifts a failed page-determinism control;
    it never forces a flow.
  - A file that is present but unusable (empty, not valid JSON, not a JSON object, "flows" of the wrong
    type, or no "flows" at all - a typo such as "flow") is IGNORED and named in the note: it forces nothing
    and clears no recorded force, so fixing it re-forces nothing. {"flows": []} lists no flow, and so does
    a file holding only unblock_repair_after_utc.
  - Never hand-edit `_flows.json`: it is compare-and-swap protected and a hand edit races a later pass.

T0 STEP (before the R2 write key is revoked): let every in-progress attempt finish, or abandon it (list the
flow in `_force_origin.json` is NOT enough - it starts a new attempt), and delete every `_repull/` chunk on
R2 - after T0 they cannot be deleted. Broken and unstable flows hold none (they delete theirs); a parked
`needs_refresh` attempt does. mirror_sync and upload_r2 carry only .parquet, so `_flows.json` and
`_force_origin.json` must be copied to the local store explicitly.

LIMITS, stated: completeness is "per INSEE paging" (no INSEE total exists); the served-parquet publish is not
conditional (two writers of one flow: last writer wins - the attempt lease protects only the repair); the
stored rows INSEE no longer serves are kept (residue, reported) until the owner decides otherwise. Memory:
classification and finalize run DuckDB under PROFILE_MEMORY_LIMIT and spill to a private directory (AR-331
F6: the earlier arrow profile peaked at 7.3 GB on DS_FLORES_A5 and 16.5 GB at 25.9M rows); the bounded
merge has its own limit. Python 3.11 (CI) runs pyarrow and duckdb here for the first time on its first run.
```

## 4. If it stops updating — diagnose in this order

Run everything from `E:\research\econfindatalibrary`.

```bash
# 1. What does the system actually say? (not what you remember)
python -c "import sys,sqlite3;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from updater import config;con=sqlite3.connect(f'file:{config.STATE_DB}?mode=ro',uri=True);print(*con.execute(\"SELECT unit_id,status,last_success_utc,last_attempt_utc,last_error FROM unit_state WHERE source_id='insee_melodi'\"),sep=chr(10))"

# 2. Is it even being ATTEMPTED? 'scheduled' is not 'attempted' (R246).
#    A daily run reaches ~20 of ~106 cloud sources; most are skipped on cadence, which is normal.
python -m updater.run --source insee_melodi --dry

# 3. Run it for real and READ THE REASON. Failures name themselves now.
AQUEDUCT_BACKEND=r2 python -u -m updater.run --source insee_melodi --force

# 4. Is the PUBLISHER healthy, or is it us? Probe upstream directly, never a relay.
#    (relay/aggregator mirrors are BANNED — every source must be reached at its own publisher.)

# 5. Is the store intact? obs_count in state is NOT the answer.
AQUEDUCT_BACKEND=r2 python -c "import sys,os;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from updater import config,blob;d=config.source_dir('insee_melodi');fs=[f for f in blob.list_parquets(d) if not os.path.basename(f).startswith('_')];print(len(fs),'files',sum(blob.row_count(os.path.join(d,os.path.basename(f))) for f in fs),'rows')"

# 6. Are its dates real? A counter-as-year or a 9999 sentinel is silent (7 sources hit).
#    NOTE: a FUTURE date is usually a legitimate projection - check the key before repairing.
python tools/audit_impossible_dates.py --r2 --source insee_melodi
```

**Read the failure class before fixing anything.** From the 2026-08-04 audit of every unfetchable source, the causes were: `budget_deferral` (NOT broken — ran out of its time slice), `code_bug`, `rate_limited`, `gated_by_design`. **Zero** were an expired credential or a dead endpoint, although that is the usual first guess.

If the error names sub-units as `deferred (budget N min)` or `budget spent`, **nothing has failed** — the source ran out of its slice and the rest is taken next tick (R303). Do not 'fix' it.

## 4b. Root cause when this was last investigated (2026-08-04)

*From the unfetchable-source audit — 29 agents, every finding challenged by a skeptic before it was accepted. This source was covered by the target `insee_melodi`.*

- **root cause**: `budget_deferral`  (confidence high)
- **which units**: ZERO of 144 failed. 15 sub-units attempted and succeeded (catalog positions 1-15, DD_CNA_AGREGATS through DS_BPE); 129 sub-units (positions 16-144) were never attempted -- the 25-minute wall-clock budget stopped the sweep before reaching them. The '129/144 transient-failed' string is a labelling artefact of the earlier code, in which the `if dl.spent():` branch called tally.transient_unit(code) instead of tally.deferred_unit(code); with the current code the same run would read '15 sub-unit(s) attempted, none failed; 129 deferred by budget and taken next tick'.
- **blast radius**: Zero rows lost or corrupted: the deferral path does `total += before` and never touches the parquet, and merge_and_write never shrinks. 36,430,103 observations across 84 parquet files remain published. The real exposure is FRESHNESS, not failure: because the budget has no rotation bookmark, the same 15-flow prefix is re-walked every tick and catalog positions 16-144 are never refreshed. Measured on the local store -- positions 1-14 last written 2026-07-25, position 15 onward last written 2026-07-14 or earlier (positions 132-144 stuck at 2026-06-10), and 65 of the 144 catalog flows have never landed at all. Status side-effect: `partial` never stamps last_success_utc (which is NULL for insee_melodi), so the source also reads as 'never succeeded'.
- fixable by us: **True**

**Recommended fix, in order:**

> Two parts; part one is already done.
> 
> (1) DONE -- do not redo. An earlier commit changed insee_melodi.py:305 from `tally.transient_unit(code)` to `tally.deferred_unit(code)` inside the `if dl.spent():` branch. The stale 129/144 state row predates it (attempt 2026-07-31T23:23:21Z). No further code change is needed for the reported symptom; the row will correct itself on the next run. If you want the queue to read true before then, re-run insee_melodi or clear that unit_state.last_error.
> 
> (2) OPEN and worth fixing -- the budget is a truncation. insee_melodi has a Deadline (BUDGET_MIN=25, insee_melodi.py:68/290) but no rotation and no per-flow freshness sidecar, so it re-walks catalog positions 1-15 forever and positions 16-144 are never fetched. Add the standard bookmark from _common.py, which is already imported in this module's neighbourhood:
>   - `bookmark = load_rotation(out_dir)` before the loop,
>   - `flows = rotate_after(flows, bookmark, key=lambda f: f.get("code",""))`,
>   - `save_rotation(out_dir, code)` after each completed flow (save on a complete pass too, so the next run wraps through the same code path).
> This is the same fix R190 applied to abs/ecb and is exactly what the Deadline docstring (_common.py:92-100) requires. Alternatively/additionally raise BUDGET_MIN for this source under AQUEDUCT_BUDGET_MIN_OVERRIDE on the workstation -- INSEE's per-flow pages are slow (one flow took 23.0 s for page 1 alone, and the ingest log shows 27+ minute flows), so 25 minutes cannot cover 144 flows in any ordering; rotation is what makes the bound honest.
> 
> Do NOT investigate INSEE as an upstream problem. api.insee.fr/melodi is healthy, keyless, and answering HTTP 200 with full 10,000-observation pages in the exact envelope the parser expects.

## 6. Rules that apply to every repair here

- **A key/parser change is a RE-PULL, never a merge** (R22). Changing what `series_key` means leaves the old and new grains coexisting; dedup cannot collapse them because they no longer collide. Use `mode="replace"`, or re-pull the table.
- **Never patch dates — re-pull** (R288). A naive date repair on `cso` would have destroyed 11 of 12 rows; only a negative control caught it. And 41,091 of `stat_slovenia`'s fabricated dates land in 1900–2200, indistinguishable from real data, so no date test can find them.
- **Verify against the store you are actually serving** (R296/R36). Under `AQUEDUCT_BACKEND=r2` the local directory is a scratch mirror of the last run only; a local check can under-report or give the opposite answer.
- **When a probe reports ABSENCE, run it against something known PRESENT** (R316). An absence looks identical whether the data is missing or the probe is broken.
- **Compare (key, date) pairs, not just keys** (R314). A re-key check that compares identifiers verifies the half you changed on purpose; the half you changed by accident is in the values.
- **A bound over a fixed order is a truncation, not a budget** (R190). If work is capped, check it ROTATES — and specifically that it rotates when the item at the head never completes (R313).
- **Read the job's ARGV, not its progress** (R323). A `--dry-run` and a real run print the same numbers.
